correctness.rationale: Direct reciprocal Brownian hitting-time Gamma law gives exact maximum-density and integrated-success expressions. Centered Gamma maxima plus uniform integrability imply Gamma(1-a) below a=1. An exact tilted-Gamma moment generating function proves the Gaussian saddle and the Phi(z/sqrt2) crossover. The regenerative Laplace transform and tilted lower bound prove the exponential completion-time scaling. The embedded verifier passed 101 finite numerical checks; these do not substitute for the analytical limit proofs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic frequent-resetting theorems can explain exponential completion after scaling by the rare-success probability; they do not by themselves give the success probability in the joint N,r_N limit or its nontrivial sharp coefficient. The older finite-N formula makes this asymptotic an extension of established machinery, not a new renewal principle.

originality.rationale: The finite-N global-resetting renewal law is fully credited to Biroli–Majumdar–Schehr (2023). Their main text and protocol-B appendix do not state the correlated joint large-population/high-rate asymptotics. Vatash et al. (2026) consider finite-N global reset comparisons and a different rank-fraction asymptotic. Linn–Lawley (2023) contain general renewal limits, not this specific population-dependent Gamma/Gumbel/Gaussian phase boundary. Claim-based searches and accessible historical statements identified no equivalent or stronger specific result; novelty is best-knowledge, not independent priority certification.
residual_risks: The complete text of every potentially relevant general high-rate first-passage theorem was not inspected; a generic asymptotic theorem may subsume some renewal arguments.
Search-result noncoverage is not mathematical proof of priority; unindexed papers or alternative Laplace-saddle formulations could predate this statement.
No independent mathematical or publication-priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The model is a natural collective search protocol supported by both a 2023 analytical study and 2026 experiments. Its singular high-rate/population competition produces a new exact threshold a=1, a Gamma-to-saddle mechanism change, a critical Gaussian amplitude, and explicit mean-time exponents. The distinction from independent resetting is structural and observable, rather than a cosmetic reformulation.
